rationale: The route WORKSPACE→CONVERSATION→MESSAGE→USER requires a single message co-satisfying authorship (Kenji Sato) and topic (supercomputer/HPC time for circuit-tracer). Base seed confirms the topic-matching message (1706112500.000001, 'Has anyone looked into getting supercomputer time for the circuit-tracer workload?') is authored by John Doe, while Kenji's only messages in the same channel (JAX prototype offer, food-logistics message) never touch the supercomputer topic. No message anywhere in the seed satisfies both conditions simultaneously, so absence is correctly grounded in a genuine missing referent rather than an access limitation. The design supplies well-targeted near-miss negatives (correct-topic/wrong-author vs. correct-author/wrong-topic) that test conflation of authorship and topic without hinting the answer. The single workspace (T01WORKSPACE) is real and the channel/message binding is well-formed; access plan (search.messages/conversations.history + users.info + conversations.info) is realistic and documented. Answer attributes (teams.team_id/team_name) are legitimate table columns. No mechanical errors, no unsupported operations, and selection mode ('one') matches the singular prompt phrasing. Wording is concise and natural, content plausible, and the trap (topic match in same channel by a different, contextually adjacent user) is meaningful without being a giveaway.
